name: b_boil1
note:
SKILL GUIDE (practice):
Goal recap: take the pot of water onto the stove, then turn the stove burner ON (the burner nearest the pot must report on).
The reward here gives partial credit: +0.5 if the pot is resting on the stove (touching it, or inside a stove region), +0.5 if any stove burner state > 0.5.

Robust pick-and-place recipe (these functions exist):
1. navigate_to("<target>") to move the mobile base so the item is in view.
2. obs = get_observation(); rgb = obs["robot0_robotview"]["images"]["rgb"]; depth = obs["robot0_robotview"]["images"]["depth"]; intr = obs["robot0_robotview"]["intrinsics"]; pose_mat = obs["robot0_robotview"]["pose_mat"].
3. mask = segment_sam3_text_prompt(rgb, "<item>")[0]["mask"]  (try several prompts; fall back to point_prompt_molmo(rgb,"<item>") and make a small mask box).
4. seg = np.zeros(mask.shape, int); seg[mask]=1; poses, scores = plan_grasp(depth, intr, seg). Take the top pose.
5. Transform the 4x4 camera-frame grasp pose: world = pose_mat @ pose. pos=world[:3,3]; R=world[:3,:3]; convert R to quat wxyz with a correct rotation->quat routine.
6. solve_ik(pos_above, down_quat) then move_to_joints; then solve_ik(pos, quat) + move_to_joints; close_gripper(); lift 0.12-0.18 m; 
7. navigate_to the target; re-observe; find the target surface with segment_sam3_text_prompt + depth unprojection (x=(u-cx)*d/fx, y=(v-cy)*d/fy, z=d; world = pose_mat @ [x,y,z,1]); move above it, descend onto it, open_gripper(); keep the gripper clear at the end.
Turn the burner ON (this is the part you previously skipped — you MUST do it):
- The stove's burner is a physical knob. Segment/point the knob (prompts: 'stove knob','burner knob','stove dial'), get its 3D position via depth unprojection, navigate so it is reachable.
- Move the gripper to the knob and TURN IT: use the best available actuation — if a knob/turn/set/rotate/set_joint function exists in the environment, call it on the knob; otherwise physically turn the knob by approaching it, grasping it and rotating the wrist, or pushing it along its arc. Try the action, then verify a burner reads on.
Do not print that you completed the task; only act. Keep each stage simple and retry perception with alternate prompts before giving up.
